newsitem.title: USA: PPG cites weaker prices, higher natgas costs.
newsitem.headline: PPG cites weaker prices, higher natgas costs.

text.p: PPG Industries Inc Thursday reported lower profits on record sales for the fourth quarter, citing lower North American auto production, weakening chemical prices and increased natural gas prices.

Pointing out that fourth quarter while earnings per share equaled the 1995 record $0.83 on fewer shares outstaninding, it said full-year sales and earnings were also records, excluding the effect of a 1995 gain from settlement of a glass technology dispute.
"All three business segments had record fourth-quarter sales, their second consecutive quarterly high," it said.

That performance was "achieved despite lower North American auto production, ongoing commodity chemicals price weakening, a dramatic increase in natural gas costs, and continued weakness in European economies," PPG said.
"Our North American businesses did well in the final quarter of the year," PPG said, "with manufacturing efficiencies contributing to overall earnings performance.
"On the other hand, the climb in natural gas prices meant higher fuel costs to generate electricity for commodity chemicals production and operate glass and fiber glass melting furnaces.
"We remain cautiously optimistic that the decline in Europe's economies may have bottomed late last year," its statement concluded. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
